Modern capitalism has been constructed by a range of players at different points in time. Accounts of its rise have often focused on the role of business leaders while the influence of less eminent contributors has often been ignored. Recent scholarship has been written to help refocus the attention to the lesser known creators of capitalism and Michael Zakim’s Accounting for Capitalism: The World the Clerk Made is a contribution to the emerging effort.
